newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia army foils rebel bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Colombia army foils rebel bomb attack.

text.p: Counter-insurgency troops foiled a suspected leftist rebel bomb attack on an airport in southern Colombia on Sunday, an army spokesman said.

Twenty-two homemade bombs, packed with dynamite, were discovered about 50 yards (metres) from the airstrip, used by civilian and military air traffic, in the town of Villagarzon in Putumayo province, Maj. Ricardo Herrera said.
He said the attack had been planned by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest guerrilla group, in order to disrupt the town's 50th anniversary celebrations.

In neighbouring Caqueta province, the demilitarization of a 5,400 square-mile (14,000 sq km) area entered the third day of a scheduled 10-day period. President Ernesto Samper ordered troops to pull out of the zone to make way for the handover of 60 troops captured by FARC fighters during an attack on a jungle base in Putumayo on August 30.
The FARC rejected government terms for the release of the captives, but Samper pinned his hopes on a seasonal show of goodwill by the rebel force.
